frontier.hypothesis: A C form in which the +4 address load has a SECOND, EARLY consumer that does not consume either of the other two 0x10 reads would put it at slot 12 in $a1 while keeping all three loads.
frontier.mechanism: A second consumer makes the load ready before its +4 consumer is scheduled, so sched2 is not starved into pinning it adjacent; but every second consumer tried so far (the +0 read, the +2 read) is itself one of the three loads, which is why paying for it costs the third load.
frontier.next_probe: Look for a use of the 0x10 pointer that target's own stream contains but the campaign has never bound to p10 - e.g. an address-arithmetic use, or a use inside the call-argument computation - and seat it early on the d8 order; measure with tmp/grind/func_80060A68/s9/run2.ps1 and diff with s9/cmp.py.

frontier.hypothesis: A pressure source that is dependent on something late in the block but consumed early would be ready at sched2's T-30 without being schedulable into forward slot 23.
frontier.mechanism: Slot 23 is a load-delay slot; any dependence-free value (idx, outer+0x18, outer+0x20) is the cheapest filler for it and takes it, which is exactly f3's and g1's 8-point cost. A value that depends on a late computation cannot be placed there.
frontier.next_probe: On the d8 order, seat a local holding a value derived from the +2 or +4 halfword (already read late) and consumed by an early store, then re-check the slot and register of every lw ?,0x10($v1) with run2.ps1.
